pattern: Of the 13 runs in this share, 9 are not model errors. They are provider-stall timeouts: CLOSURE-23-MPO-001 x3, LANG-1-MPO-001 x3, LANG-34-MPO-001 x2 and GSON-1-DISC-001 run-001. Each trajectory ends on a tool output with 0-5 API calls and no submission, the wall times are 348-1051 s against a 300 s limit, and one run (CLOSURE-23 run-011) never wrote a trajectory. These should be excluded rather than counted as misses. In 4 of them (GSON run-001, LANG-1 runs 002 and 013) the gold body had already been displayed before the stall. The manifest gold_file_read metric is unreliable for this purpose: it says false for GSON run-001 although ObjectTypePair was fully shown, and true for LANG-34 run-006 although appendEnd was skipped. All 4 scored misses (gold ranks 2, 2, 3, 7) are attribution failures, not search failures. In every one the agent read the gold body in full, ran the failing test, saw the failure values and named the gold in its evidence_chain. In the two DISP runs (COMPRESS-8, LANG-5) the agent explicitly says the delegate holds the concrete defect but still ranks the test-called public facade first (entry-point / contract-owner preference). In the two OWN runs the agent places a co-participant in the same mechanism above the gold: the caller that encodes null (CLOSURE-12, computeMayUse) and the decision site that reads the shared table (CLOSURE-131, isSimpleNameChars). This happens even though the convention evidence was fetched both times, and in CLOSURE-131 it was explicitly cited. So in split-ownership designs the agent finds the mechanism but assigns it to the more salient caller or reader rather than the method that actually violates the convention.
